headline: Southborough set its FY27 tax rate at $14.54 while municipal and school boards confronted a projected $1.4 million FY28 operating deficit.
synopsis: In November, Southborough finalized its FY27 single property tax rate of $14.54 as town and school officials turned their focus to a looming FY28 budget deficit. Town administration forecast a $1.4 million shortfall under level services, initiating discussions on whether to propose a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override or order deep department spending cuts. Meanwhile, the School Committee reviewed a preliminary 5.36 percent budget increase driven by surges in special education tuition and student transportation costs. In school infrastructure, the Neary Elementary School roof replacement neared completion nearly $1.6 million under budget, while officials debated whether to pursue state assistance for a comprehensive building renovation. Additionally, the Planning Board continued reviewing traffic congestion around the proposed Route 9 Costco warehouse, and the DPW presented requests for smart water meters and tank repairs.

top_items.title: Town evaluates override options for projected $1.4 million FY28 deficit
top_items.why: Early projections for FY28 show a $1.4 million shortfall under level municipal services, prompting town leaders to weigh an operational override against service cuts.
top_items.body: Town administration outlined two distinct paths for the FY28 budget: Budget A maintains level services but requires a Proposition 2 1/2 override to cover a $1.4 million deficit, while Budget B level-funds department budgets by requiring staff and service reductions. The Select Board scheduled budget hearings with large departments and instructed officials to prepare impact memos explaining the operational consequences of proposed cuts.

top_items.title: School Committee reviews preliminary 5.36% FY28 budget increase
top_items.why: Rising costs for out-of-district special education and student transportation pushed the preliminary K-8 school operating budget up by $1.4 million.
top_items.body: District administrators presented a preliminary FY28 budget of $27,514,571, an increase of $1,399,853 driven by a 41 percent rise in special education tuitions and a 13 percent increase in transportation costs. The Southborough School Committee discussed options to meet town guidance, noting that a level-funded budget would require cutting $1.4 million and approximately 15 staff positions.

top_items.title: Select Board adopts single FY27 property tax rate of $14.54
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to keep a uniform tax rate for residential and commercial properties, rejecting rate split and exemption proposals.
top_items.body: Southborough's total property valuation reached $4.072 billion for FY27, with the average single-family home valuation increasing by 3.7 percent to $1,027,800. Following the tax classification hearing, the board voted 4-1 to set a single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand and voted 5-0 against adopting residential or small commercial exemptions.

top_items.title: Neary School renovation designs advance amid debate over state funding
top_items.why: Architects presented refined addition and renovation plans for Neary School while officials weighed whether to enter the multi-year MSBA funding process.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects unveiled refined designs for Option 3, which includes a secure entry, an expanded gymnasium in the interior courtyard, new breakout learning spaces, and the elimination of modular classrooms. The School Committee discussed whether to submit a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority in January 2027 or fund the project locally to avoid multi-year scheduling delays and construction cost inflation.

top_items.title: Planning Board questions traffic impacts for proposed Costco warehouse
top_items.why: Costco presented a revised traffic study for its 167,000-square-foot warehouse and gas station, facing concerns over local traffic congestion.
top_items.body: Planning Board members and residents scrutinized projected traffic impacts, focusing on failing intersection service levels along Route 9 and potential truck traffic cutting through residential neighborhoods. Costco offered mitigation plans including repaving Coslin Drive and Crystal Pond Road, traffic signal timing adjustments, and travel demand programs before the hearing was continued to November 16.

top_items.title: DPW presents $1.82 million smart water meter capital request
top_items.why: The Department of Public Works proposed digital water meters to address an estimated 20 percent water loss, along with tank maintenance and vehicle requests.
top_items.body: Public works officials outlined major FY28 capital priorities to the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee, including $1.82 million for advanced smart water meters, $700,000 for state-mandated repairs to the Tara Road water tank, and $550,000 for two highway plow trucks. The DPW also noted ongoing evaluations of an $823,000 soil cleanup at the former Atwood tank site.

top_items.title: Neary School roof replacement wraps up $1.6 million under budget
top_items.why: The Neary roof replacement reached 97 percent completion, projecting final costs of roughly $2.91 million against a $4.5 million appropriation.
top_items.body: School administrators reported that the Neary roof project has entered punch-list completion well below its original budget. The unused borrowing authorization of nearly $1.6 million will be returned to reduce the town's overall debt burden.
